title: Boss: charged twice after a deploy
summary: An incident ticket: double charges during a rolling deploy. Fix the key, the offsets, the handler and the downstream pipeline.

steps.title: INC-4127: customers charged twice after the 14:05 deploy
body: **INC-4127 · Sev 2 · billing** · opened by Support, assigned to you
37 customers have two card charges for one order. Every affected order was paid between 14:05 and 14:09, during the
rolling deploy of `billing-worker` (6 pods, Confluent.Kafka, `EnableAutoCommit = true`, defaults otherwise).
14:05:12.031 billing-worker-5 INFO  Charged o-88213 1299 provider_key=0f9c2e71 ch_8812
14:05:19.902 billing-worker-2 INFO  Charged o-88213 1299 provider_key=a41be093 ch_8830
GROUP    TOPIC               PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG  CONSUMER-ID
Worker 5 exited without `Close()`, the last auto-commit was seconds old, so the new owner redelivered 111 records.
The provider key is a fresh GUID per attempt, so the provider charged again.
1. The provider idempotency key is stable for an order, whatever the attempt or message id.
2. Offsets are committed only up to the last record actually finished.
3. A redelivered message never charges again, even if the pod died after the provider call.
4. The `payments-charged` to `payments-ledger` projector is exactly-once inside Kafka.

steps.title: 1. A stable provider key
prompt: `ProviderKey` is sent to the payment provider as its idempotency key. The provider charges once per key. Today it
returns a new random value on every call, so every redelivery is a new charge.
Fix it so the key depends **only on the order**: return `"charge-{orderId}"`, whatever `messageId` and `attempt` are.
starter: string ProviderKey(string orderId, string messageId, int attempt)
solution: string ProviderKey(string orderId, string messageId, int attempt)
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("the key for o-88213", "charge-o-88213", ProviderKey("o-88213", "m-1", 1));
Dojo.Eq("same key on a redelivery", ProviderKey("o-88213", "m-1", 1), ProviderKey("o-88213", "m-1", 2));
Dojo.Eq("same key for a different message about the same order", ProviderKey("o-88213", "m-1", 1), ProviderKey("o-88213", "m-9", 1));
Dojo.Check("different orders get different keys", ProviderKey("o-1", "m-1", 1) != ProviderKey("o-2", "m-1", 1), "two orders share a key");

forbid.message: No random part in the key

steps.title: 2. Commit only what is finished
prompt: The worker now processes a polled batch in parallel and commits by hand. Write
`long OffsetToCommit(long committed, long[] offsets, bool[] done)`:
- `offsets` are the batch's record offsets, ascending (gaps are normal: compaction and transaction markers use
offsets too); `done[i]` says whether record `i` has finished.
- Return the offset to commit: **the offset after the last record of the unbroken run of finished records from the
start of the batch**. If the first record is not finished (or the batch is empty) return `committed` unchanged.
```text
committed 10, offsets [10, 11, 13, 14], done [T, T, T, F]  →  14
committed 10, offsets [10, 11, 13, 14], done [T, F, T, T]  →  11   (13 and 14 will be redelivered: fine, the handler is idempotent)
starter: long OffsetToCommit(long committed, long[] offsets, bool[] done)
solution: long OffsetToCommit(long committed, long[] offsets, bool[] done)
hints: Walk the batch from the start; stop at the first `done[i] == false`.
Each finished record moves the answer to `offsets[i] + 1`, not `i + 1`.
template: {{CODE}}
Dojo.Eq("stops before the first unfinished record", 14L, OffsetToCommit(10, new long[] { 10, 11, 13, 14 }, new[] { true, true, true, false }));
Dojo.Eq("a hole in the middle holds the commit back", 11L, OffsetToCommit(10, new long[] { 10, 11, 13, 14 }, new[] { true, false, true, true }));
Dojo.Eq("first record unfinished: commit nothing new", 10L, OffsetToCommit(10, new long[] { 10, 11 }, new[] { false, true }));
Dojo.Eq("all finished: the offset after the last record", 15L, OffsetToCommit(10, new long[] { 10, 11, 13, 14 }, new[] { true, true, true, true }));
Dojo.Eq("an empty batch", 10L, OffsetToCommit(10, new long[0], new bool[0]));

steps.title: 3. A billing handler that survives the crash
prompt: Write a class `Billing` that combines the inbox with the provider key.
- `Billing(PaymentProvider provider)`. The tests define `PaymentProvider` with
`string Charge(string idempotencyKey, int cents)`: it returns a charge id (`ch_1`, `ch_2`, ...) and charges only
once per key (a repeated key returns the original charge id).
- `string Handle(string messageId, string orderId, int cents, bool crashAfterCharge = false)`:
1. `messageId` already processed → `"duplicate"`;
2. `orderId` already charged by an earlier message → record `messageId` as processed, return `"already charged"`;
3. call `provider.Charge("charge-{orderId}", cents)`;
4. if `crashAfterCharge` → the pod died before the database commit: record nothing, return `"crashed"`;
5. otherwise record the message and the order, add `"{orderId} {chargeId}"` to `Ledger`, return `"charged {chargeId}"`.
- `List<string> Ledger` (get-only).
The card charge cannot be inside your database transaction; the stable key is what makes the retry after step 4 safe.
starter: public string Handle(string messageId, string orderId, int cents, bool crashAfterCharge = false) => "";
solution: public string Handle(string messageId, string orderId, int cents, bool crashAfterCharge = false)
hints: Two sets: processed message ids and paid order ids.
On `crashAfterCharge` return before touching either set or the ledger: nothing was committed.
template: var dojoP = new PaymentProvider();
var dojoB = new Billing(dojoP);
Dojo.Eq("first charge", "charged ch_1", dojoB.Handle("m-1", "o-88213", 1299));
Dojo.Eq("redelivered after the rebalance", "duplicate", dojoB.Handle("m-1", "o-88213", 1299));
Dojo.Eq("the pod dies after the provider call", "crashed", dojoB.Handle("m-2", "o-88214", 500, crashAfterCharge: true));
Dojo.Eq("the new partition owner retries and gets the same charge", "charged ch_2", dojoB.Handle("m-2", "o-88214", 500));
Dojo.Eq("the provider charged each order once", 1799, dojoP.TotalCharged);
Dojo.Eq("the provider was called three times", 3, dojoP.Calls);
Dojo.Eq("a second message for a paid order", "already charged", dojoB.Handle("m-3", "o-88213", 1299));
Dojo.Eq("no provider call for an order already paid", 3, dojoP.Calls);
Dojo.Eq("its redelivery is a duplicate", "duplicate", dojoB.Handle("m-3", "o-88213", 1299));
Dojo.Eq("ledger", new List<string> { "o-88213 ch_1", "o-88214 ch_2" }, dojoB.Ledger);
{{CODE}}
class PaymentProvider
readonly Dictionary<string, (string Id, int Cents)> byKey = new();
public int Calls { get; private set; }
public int TotalCharged => byKey.Values.Sum(c => c.Cents);
public string Charge(string idempotencyKey, int cents)
Calls++;
if (byKey.TryGetValue(idempotencyKey, out var existing)) return existing.Id;
var id = $"ch_{byKey.Count + 1}";
byKey[idempotencyKey] = (id, cents);
return id;

steps.title: 4. An exactly-once projector inside Kafka
prompt: The `ledger-projector` reads `payments-charged` and writes `payments-ledger`. Model Kafka's transactional log so the
team can test the projector's commit logic. Write a class `TxLog`:
- `void Begin()`: opens a transaction; throws `InvalidOperationException` if one is already open.
- `void Produce(string value)`: appends a record **to the log immediately** (Kafka writes it, the transaction marker
decides visibility); throws `InvalidOperationException` when no transaction is open.
- `void SendOffsets(long nextOffset)`: the input offset to commit **with** this transaction; throws when none is open.
- `void Commit()`: marks the transaction committed and, if offsets were sent, sets `CommittedOffset`; throws when
none is open.
- `void Abort()`: marks it aborted; its records stay in the log; `CommittedOffset` does not move; throws when none is open.
- `List<string> ReadCommitted()`: records of committed transactions only, in log order.
- `List<string> ReadUncommitted()`: every record in the log, in order (what a default consumer sees).
- `long CommittedOffset` (starts at 0).
starter: public long CommittedOffset { get; private set; }
solution: readonly List<(string Value, int Tx)> records = new();
public long CommittedOffset { get; private set; }
if (current != 0) throw new InvalidOperationException("a transaction is already open");
public List<string> ReadCommitted() => records.Where(r => state[r.Tx] == "committed").Select(r => r.Value).ToList();
if (current == 0) throw new InvalidOperationException("no open transaction");
hints: Tag every record with the id of the transaction that wrote it, and keep a state per transaction id.
`ReadCommitted` filters records by their transaction's state; `ReadUncommitted` does not filter.
Keep the offset sent in this transaction aside, and copy it to `CommittedOffset` only in `Commit`.
template: var dojoT = new TxLog();
dojoT.Begin(); dojoT.Produce("o-1 charged"); dojoT.SendOffsets(1); dojoT.Commit();
Dojo.Eq("a committed transaction is visible", new List<string> { "o-1 charged" }, dojoT.ReadCommitted());
Dojo.Eq("its offset moved with it", 1L, dojoT.CommittedOffset);
dojoT.Begin(); dojoT.Produce("o-2 charged"); dojoT.SendOffsets(2);
Dojo.Eq("open transaction: read_committed does not see it", new List<string> { "o-1 charged" }, dojoT.ReadCommitted());
Dojo.Eq("open transaction: the offset is not committed yet", 1L, dojoT.CommittedOffset);
dojoT.Abort();
Dojo.Eq("aborted: still invisible to read_committed", new List<string> { "o-1 charged" }, dojoT.ReadCommitted());
Dojo.Eq("aborted: read_uncommitted sees the aborted record", new List<string> { "o-1 charged", "o-2 charged" }, dojoT.ReadUncommitted());
Dojo.Eq("aborted: the input offset stays where it was", 1L, dojoT.CommittedOffset);
dojoT.Begin(); dojoT.Produce("o-2 charged"); dojoT.SendOffsets(2); dojoT.Commit();
Dojo.Eq("the retry is visible exactly once", new List<string> { "o-1 charged", "o-2 charged" }, dojoT.ReadCommitted());
Dojo.Eq("output and offset moved together", 2L, dojoT.CommittedOffset);
Dojo.Eq("the log itself holds three records", 3, dojoT.ReadUncommitted().Count);
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("produce outside a transaction", () => dojoT.Produce("x"));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("commit with nothing open", () => dojoT.Commit());
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("abort with nothing open", () => dojoT.Abort());
dojoT.Begin();
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("begin twice", () => dojoT.Begin());
{{CODE}}
